events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip was cancelled by the driver at 09:54:25, and the driver asserts a rider no-show, so the fee's validity runs through NS-0 → NS-1 [F4][F13][NS-0]. The NS-1 elements are met on the record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, and the GPS shows he was 42 m from the pickup at that moment (closest approach 38 m), i.e. within the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. He then remained inside that radius until cancellation — 3 min 40 s (220 s) after the tap, more than the 3-minute threshold — so the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee is prima facie established [F6][F5][NS-1].

However, the SAFETY SCREEN overrides the fee analysis. Reading the chat in context rather than by keyword: message #3 at 09:54 from the driver reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F11]. This is not a pickup arrangement or a route remark; it is a direct threat of personal consequence aimed at the rider, sent one minute before the driver cancelled, and the rider's own complaint expressly alleges that the driver threatened them [F11][F4]. Ryde's code of conduct bars "Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind", including "Threats and Intimidation" [SAFE-1]. That makes this more than a rude message: the safety screen comes out "confirmed", and a case with a confirmed SAFE-1 concern must not be auto-decided — it goes to a human reviewer with a factual summary [SAFE-1]. The chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped) so there is no RD-5-style timing ambiguity to resolve [F12].

Because the safety screen is confirmed, I do not rule on the fee: the ruling is escalate, amount null [SAFE-1]. I note, without deciding, that if the fee issue were reached on its own, NS-1 would support no_action, and no flag_account arises on that branch because no clause calls for it (NS-1 gives no_action). Whether the rider's account should also be reviewed is for the human reviewer, since the driver may have had a genuine no-show before the threat [F13][F10][NS-1].
